sources.priorKnowledge: This course builds on the first-year finance and accounting courses EBC1025 and EBC1037/EBC1038/EBC1039 and the topics covered in these courses and their content are thus prerequisites. In particular: Students are expected to understand the following finance concepts: Types of securities (stocks, bonds) and their returns; Markowitz’ portfolio theory (risk-return relationships, efficient frontier, security market line), CAPM (capital market line, beta); definitions and implications of market efficiency; principles of time value of money; converting accounting figures into cash flows; capital budgeting including NPV, IRR. Students are expected to be familiar with core concepts from the first-year financial accounting course, including financial statements, their main items, and their interrelationships. This knowledge is required to follow and apply the finance and accounting topics covered in this course.An advanced level of English is required.

curriculum: The English-taught International Business BSc uses the regular route without Emerging Markets. Each of the first two years is 60 EC with eight 6.5 EC courses and two 4 EC skills trainings. Year 2 includes compulsory Quantitative Methods III and one choice from the approved skills list. The published regular-route Year 3 template totals 60 EC: 26 EC exchange, 13 EC chosen within one major, 6.5 EC from the specified elective lists, two 2 EC professional development units, 2.5 EC thesis skills and 8 EC individual thesis. The 2026–27 EER publishes both generic and named major outlines. The general pathway retains the restricted slots. Named exceptions in Accounting and Entrepreneurship have separate rules, and Accounting variant 2 has an internal wording discrepancy between article and table which is outside the selected generic template. Emerging Markets has distinct years 2 and 3, including a 19.5 EC internship and 10.5 EC thesis.
progression: The first-year study phases place Quantitative Methods I before II and both before the case-based Quantitative Methods III. The Management Game follows foundational business courses. Managerial Finance and Accounting builds on first-year Finance and Accounting; Marketing Management and Management of Organisations build on the first-year management course. The generic first exchange option uses Semester 5 and Global Citizenship Skills, then the two major courses, restricted elective, thesis skills, Leadership Skills and individual thesis in Semester 6. The approved partner exchange requires 53.5 EC of Year 1 to apply and 60 EC before departure. At least 19.5 EC of exchange courses must be field-related. Article 12.1 confirms that the thesis is an individual academic paper. The published generic outline avoids the variant-specific restrictions.
components: Quantitative Methods III (EBS2001, compulsory skills training)
Management of Operations and Product Development (EBC2022)
Choose a skills course from Maastricht’s approved fourth-semester list.
Study abroad semester at a partner university
The regular route requires 26 EC of approved study abroad. Students need at least 53.5 EC from Year 1 to apply and all 60 EC before departure.
First course in the chosen major

Choose two courses from one approved business major. Maastricht publishes options in accounting, finance, information management, supply chain management, marketing, organisation, strategy and entrepreneurship.
Second course in the chosen major
Take the second course from the same major. Maastricht specifies separate arrangements for some majors.
Choose one course from the approved quantitative economics, economics, ethics or law lists.
Writing a Bachelor's Thesis (EBS2080, thesis skills training)
The 2.5 EC skills course prepares students for the individual thesis.
The required thesis is an individual academic research paper worth 8 EC.
